public_rationale: Microsoft's April 29, 2026 release for the quarter ended March 31 reported an AI annual revenue run rate above $37 billion [e1]. This is an annualized measure for one company before the forecast period, so it does not establish the assumed $70 billion in combined realized annual AI revenue [e1]. The disclosure also does not establish the $900 billion investment baseline or provide recovery accounts testing whether each company needs more than $100 billion in annual AI revenue [e1]. It supplies no qualifying early-resolution evidence for the claim's horizon ending May 19, 2027 [e1].
limitations: The May 19, 2027 deadline is after the October 28, 2026 evaluation date.
The investment baseline, its allocation among companies and the combined realized-revenue premise remain unverified.
A revenue milestone alone cannot establish necessity or investment recovery; costs, margins and prior recoveries are missing.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: To pay off investments now totaling over $900 billion, Microsoft, Google and Amazon will each need to be making over $100 billion in AI revenue in the next year, and doubling or tripling their best-case combined $70 billion in annual AI revenue won't be enough.
conditions: to pay off over $900 billion in investments
assuming the best-case $70 billion combined current revenue

statement.excerpt: Doubling that won’t be enough. Tripling it won’t be enough. In fact, to pay this off, these companies will need to be making over $100 billion each in AI revenue in the next year, because otherwise there is no covering these losses.

from_speaker: over $100 billion each in AI revenue
a combined $70 billion in annual revenue
our_interpretation: This asserts a necessary revenue level for investment recovery. It does not predict that each company will actually reach that level.
Read the next year as the twelve months following publication, ending May 19, 2027.
Read revenue as realized annual AI revenue because the surrounding text explicitly distinguishes run rates from revenues.
The stated investment and current-revenue premises must be established on consistent definitions before scoring the conditional claim.
Payoff requires an investment-recovery account. Revenue alone cannot establish recovery without costs, margins, prior recoveries, and the investment allocation among companies.
The speaker's aggregate figures are estimates, rather than a stated GAAP or company-reported AI segment measure.
criteria.support_condition: With the stated premises established, comparable investment-recovery accounts show that each company required more than $100 billion in annual AI revenue within the horizon, and that doubling or tripling the stated combined revenue was insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: With the premises established, at least one company demonstrably recovers its relevant investment without exceeding $100 billion in annual AI revenue within the horizon, or matching accounts show recovery possible at the stated doubled or tripled combined revenue.
